title: Who Should Be Given Incentives? Counterfactual Optimal Treatment Regimes Learning for Recommendation

problem.claim: The paper addresses personalized incentive allocation under a limited budget to improve user experience and platform revenue.

gap.claim: Prior uplift-modeling approaches may fail to identify and predict Always Buyers, who purchase regardless of incentives and may consume incentives unnecessarily.

contributions.claim: The paper divides users into five strata from an individual counterfactual perspective and proposes principled counterfactual identification and estimation methods.
The paper proposes a counterfactual entire-space multi-task learning approach for personalized incentive policy learning under a limited budget.
The paper derives a lower bound on the reward of the learned policy.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on three real-world datasets covering two incentive scenarios.
The authors report that the experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approaches.
The authors state that the counterfactual identification and estimation methods are unbiased.

narrative_sequence.summary: Personalized incentives are framed as potentially beneficial to both users and e-commerce platforms.
Prior work estimates conditional average treatment effects and allocates incentives by maximizing estimated treatment effects under a budget.
Always Buyers can make prior allocation strategies irrational because they purchase without incentives and may actively use them when offered.
The paper introduces counterfactual user strata, principled identification and estimation, and an entire-space multi-task learning approach for policy learning.
The paper derives a reward lower bound and reports experiments on three real-world datasets across two incentive scenarios.

source_observation.claim: Users who purchase regardless of treatment may still consume incentives if they receive them.

interpretation.claim: Treatment allocation should distinguish persuadable users from users whose outcome is insensitive to treatment.

application.claim: Incentive systems can use counterfactual user strata to reduce delivery to Always Buyers under budget constraints.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported approach generalizes beyond the stated incentive scenarios or datasets.

source_observation.claim: The proposed policy-learning approach is designed for a limited budget and is accompanied by a theoretically derived reward lower bound.

interpretation.claim: Resource-constrained treatment policies can benefit from combining counterfactual modeling with explicit performance guarantees.

application.claim: Budgeted recommendation or intervention systems may evaluate policies using both counterfactual estimates and conservative reward bounds.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the assumptions, form, or tightness of the lower bound.

unknowns: The five user strata are not individually defined.
The abstract does not name the three datasets or specify their sizes.
The two incentive scenarios are not described.
Evaluation metrics and comparative baselines are not specified.
The assumptions and proof details behind unbiasedness and the reward lower bound are omitted.
